A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ToaD research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and relocated or renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original benchmark comparisons and univariate and multivariate penalty-sensitivity experiments.

after.justification: The original empirical study is retained, with additional random-forest comparisons and measured microcontroller inference times in Appendices D and E.1.

M1.justification: The feature and threshold penalties, modified split gain, pointer-free encoding and shared value arrays remain unchanged. Appendix A retains the same derivation. Parameter renaming and prototype deployment do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: The eight tabular prediction benchmarks in Table 1 are unchanged. Appendix E.1 adds actual deployment tests on XIAO ESP32S3 and Arduino Nano 33 BLE hardware, using randomized inputs to a binary-Covertype model, extending test-environment coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 4 adds array-based, pointer-free LightGBM alongside the retained LightGBM, quantized LightGBM, CEGB and CCP comparators. New Figure 8 additionally evaluates standard random forests and forests pruned using Guo et al. (2018), substantially broadening the comparisons.

E3.justification: The main hyperparameter grid and 80/20 split ratio remain. New protocols include a classification comparison capped at 256 trees and hardware latency evaluation of a 0.5 KB, four-tree, depth-four model using 500 randomized-input predictions per run. Section 4.3 also corrects the stated reuse-factor ratio; newly disclosed validation details do not establish that the earlier protocol changed.

E4.justification: The array-based LightGBM control tests whether benefits extend beyond removing pointers, and Section 4.4 adds a quantitative dominance analysis. Most existing sensitivity analyses are retained, but v1 Figure 25, covering 1,024 iterations and depth 8 in the multivariate analysis, is omitted.

E5.justification: Unlike v1's curves without uncertainty reporting, v2 Figure 4 reports means and standard deviations over 12 train-test splits, with seeds 1–12 specified. Appendix E.1 also reports 20 timing runs and a variance-based stopping rationale. These substantially expand statistical reporting; v1 does not establish its original run count.

E6.justification: Figure 4 replaces the earlier curves with split-averaged results and adds the array-based comparator; Figure 8 adds random-forest results. Table 2 newly reports ToaD versus LightGBM latencies of 137.08 versus 17.63 microseconds on ESP32S3 and 512.89 versus 102.16 on Arduino. Section 4.4 adds the 3.37% dominated-solutions finding, while the final multivariate sensitivity grid is removed. These are revised or additional results, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 changes the reuse-factor definition from global values divided by nodes plus leaves to its reciprocal, consistent with the stated reuse interpretation. This corrects a mathematical definition beyond merely renaming RF to ReF. The training equations and Appendix A derivation are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement and conclusion retain the same central claims: compression through reuse-promoting penalties and specialized storage, with comparable predictive performance and reported 4–16-fold compression. New experiments support or qualify these claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds qualifications concerning complete versus incomplete trees, random forests' multiclass advantages, and dataset-dependent penalty-search heuristics. It also interprets the measured 5–8-fold prototype slowdown as practically negligible because sensing and communication dominate, although end-to-end latency and energy measurements are not supplied.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the anonymous-code access information with a named repository and specifies release v1.0.0 and LightGBM 4.6.0. It newly documents five-fold validation for the two smallest datasets, validation holdouts for larger datasets, the PALMA II computing resource, and hardware/prototype details and access instructions. These materially strengthen reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 and Appendix C add targeted coverage of FPGA quantization, bit-level GBDT training, forest pruning/refinement and resource-efficient nearest-neighbor models. The central positioning around training-time feature and threshold reuse remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative are retained. v2 adds a baseline-results subsection, reproducibility statement and acknowledgments, reorganizes the appendices around the new experiments, and updates author information, publication headers and terminology.

P2.justification: Figure 4 gains reordered panels, an expanded legend and uncertainty displays; Figures 5–7 are reformatted. v2 adds Figure 8 and Table 2 and redistributes the retained appendix plots while omitting v1 Figure 25. The method schematics and most sensitivity displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 materially strengthens empirical credibility through split-level uncertainty reporting and a pointer-free LightGBM control that addresses a central comparison weakness. Random-forest comparisons, measured deployment costs and substantially clearer reproducibility information further improve assessability. These gains outweigh the omitted sensitivity grid. The claim that the measured slowdown has negligible overall latency or energy impact remains insufficiently tested.
